newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken says capital ratio not too high.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken says capital ratio not too high.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken said on Friday its large capital ratio was not too strong as it planned to be aggressive in the Nordic and Baltic areas and in information technology in the future.
"We have a very strong capital ratio even after the spin-off of Diligentia," the bank's chief executive Bjorn Svedberg told a news conference after the bank released its 1996 earnings.
"Many think it is too strong, but I don't. We will be aggressive and expand in the Nordic and Baltic area as well as on the IT side."
For 1996, S-E-Banken reported a total capital ratio of 12.7 percent, down from 15.2 percent in 1995 and a core capital ratio of 6.9 percent, down from 9.6.
The bank said the fall was mainly due to the distribution of real estate company Diligentia to shareholders in September, 1996, which reduced group equity by seven billion crowns.
"(It was) also due to the fact that the capital requirements comprise interest rate, currency and share price risks as from 1996 in addition to credit risks," the bank said in a statement.
The spin-off to a large extent also explains S-E-Banken's lower market share on loans to large corporations in 1996, the bank's controller Urban Jarneld said.
"You have to remember that in absolute figures, we increased our lending in 1996," Jarneld told Reuters at the news conference.
"The spin-off of Diligentia means that other banks gave credits to Diligentia - previously we financed the entire company with 15 billion crowns."
In its earnings statement, the bank did not specify how large a market share it holds in the sector of loans to large companies but said its total corporate lending market share was 27 percent.
